requirements.evidence: All four routes and contract codes are present (routes/api.php:9-15); pairing format/401/success with locked transaction at app/Http/Controllers/Totem/TotemAuthController.php:23-92; JWT/totem/preset/entity validation and queue intersection at app/Http/Middleware/TotemAuth.php:53-108; queues/priorities/ticket payloads at app/Http/Controllers/Totem/TotemController.php:25-120; migration, models, factories, command, config, phpunit secret and docs all updated. Edge gaps: no retry when a random login_code collides (TotemPairingCode.php:36-42) and malformed-code attempts are not audited (TotemAuthController.php:23).

conventions.evidence: Reversible generated-style migration with down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_totem_tables.php:1-53), deliberate fillable attributes on both models, domain write reuses App\Actions\IssueTicket (TotemController.php:86-105), docs updated in the same change. Deviations: CHANGELOG.md gets no [Unreleased] entry, and the new public controller/command methods carry no method-level PHPDoc.

security.evidence: JWT verification checks the algorithm, uses hash_equals and validates exp (app/Totem/TotemJwt.php:54-92); every auth failure maps to 401 (TotemAuth.php:53-72); entity and queue authorization is server-side (TotemController.php:143-168). Gap: secret() coerces a missing TOTEM_JWT_SECRET to '' (TotemJwt.php:17-19), so a misconfigured deployment accepts tokens signed with an empty key.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/TotemApiTest.php:50-437 covers the pairing command, 400/401 cases, JWT claims, last_seen_at, scope intersection, 403/404, priorities, sequential issuance A001/A002, CORS and the pairing 429. Not covered: the ticket 30/min throttle and its rate_limited response, plus the command's printed code and audit entry.

simplicity.evidence: Small focused controllers/middleware that reuse IssueTicket; no service or repository layer. Minor baggage: services.totem.web_origin is added but never read because config/cors.php reads TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN directly (config/services.php:43-46), and the preset queue-id pluck is duplicated (TotemAuth.php:76-80, TotemAuthController.php:52-55).

readability.evidence: Clear names, small typed methods, class/helper docblocks and consistent formatting across app/Http/Controllers/Totem/TotemController.php:25-168, app/Http/Middleware/TotemAuth.php:30-108 and app/Totem/TotemJwt.php:1-109; the backend-owned priorities live in one readable class (app/Totem/TotemPriorities.php:10-66).

scope.evidence: Every touched file serves the task: env, command, controllers, middleware, JWT/priority helpers, bootstrap wiring, CORS, config, factories, migration, docs, phpunit and tests; there are no unrelated refactors or unrelated files.

issues.explanation: When TOTEM_JWT_SECRET is unset the signing key becomes an empty string, so tokens signed with that empty key verify and anyone could forge a totem JWT; the helper should fail fast (or refuse to sign/verify) when the secret is missing or too short.
The 6-digit regex uses a $ anchor that also matches a trailing newline, so a code like "123456\n" falls through to the 401 path instead of the required 400 invalid_code_format.
Malformed-code requests return before any audit write, so these pairing failures are never recorded although the task requires auditing pairing success and failure.
A random code that collides with another preset's unique login_code makes save() throw a query exception, yielding a 500 instead of retrying a fresh code.
Only the pairing throttle is exercised; the ticket endpoint's 30/min throttle and its 429 rate_limited JSON are untested, and the command test does not assert the printed code or audit entry.
The change syncs three docs but adds no [Unreleased] CHANGELOG entry, and the new public controller and command methods have no method-level PHPDoc as the docs convention asks.

The updated contract still says failed attempts are limited "per code + per IP", while the implementation only throttles by IP via throttle:10,1, so the doc describes behaviour that is not implemented.
services.totem.web_origin is added but nothing reads it (config/cors.php reads TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN directly), leaving a dead second source of truth for the same setting.

REMOTE_ADDR is passed in the headers array (transformed to HTTP_REMOTE_ADDR) and the $ip state is not shared with the helper, so the varied client IPs never reach the throttle key and the tests only isolate because the array cache resets per test.

review.summary: This implements the totem BFF end to end: pairing command and login endpoint, HS256 JWT plus the totem.auth middleware, the three authenticated endpoints with backend-owned priorities, CORS, migrations/models/factories, docs and an extensive Pest suite, reusing IssueTicket as required. The contract is met and the tests are broad, but the JWT helper accepts an empty signing key when TOTEM_JWT_SECRET is unset, which would let anyone forge tokens, so I would add a fail-fast secret guard plus the small audit/collision/doc/test gaps before merging.
